guest.titre: Chartered Financial Planner, Property Developer, Author, Podcast Host and Seasoned Investor
guest.bio_context: Nicole Bremner is a chartered financial planner and property developer with over two decades of experience navigating financial services across Sydney, London and New York. She has pioneered property crowdfunding initiatives and orchestrated multi-million pound investments. Her journey includes building and losing a multi-million pound property portfolio, documented in her debut book Bricked It, and she has recovered from significant personal losses including her marriage, home, and identity, while managing ongoing legal battles.

context.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to the Prosperity Podcast with me, Nicole Bremner, an investor and entrepreneur. Along with discussions around investing, I'm currently serializing my book Bricked It, the story of building and losing a multi-million pound property portfolio. Let's get into it. Conclusion, what to do next. I've thrown a lot at you in this book. That's kind of the goal. I want to give you a fail safe system to quickly appraise every opportunity that comes your way, a system that assists you to make safer decisions. This safer system was born out of my painful experience after nearly losing everything. You may recall that I lost my marriage, my home, my friends, and my identity. It has taken years to build back up from that. While I'm still fighting legal battles, I'm confident that I'll make a near full recovery financially, but it has taken a heavy toll on my health and my relationships. I don't want you to go through the pain that I did. If I'd had this system and kept to it, I would not have wasted the first five years of my forties wallowing in self-pity and anguish. Even if it can help just one of you reading this book, it will have been worth the effort of writing it. In part one, we explored the challenges that can derail even experienced investors. And we walked through a personal assessment of your goals, mindset, and current financial habits. You learned how to identify your unique strengths and weaknesses, recognize the warning signs of risky thinking, and lay the groundwork for an intentional approach to investing. In part two, we unpacked the safer system itself, a proven step-by-step framework to guide every investment decision you make. You learned how to create a clear strategy, acquire investments wisely, fund them safely, plan multiple exit options, and review and repeat what works. Each stage was illustrated with real life examples so you can see how to apply the safer principles to your own situation. In part three, you rolled up your sleeves to get practical. You identified exactly where you stand today by calculating your net worth, analyzing your income and expenditure, and placing yourself in one of three investor categories, small, medium, or large. You then explored tailored strategies for each stage so you know the next steps, whether you're starting with 5,000 pounds or 500,000 pounds. You've been equipped with the tools, knowledge, and mindset to approach every investment opportunity safer and smarter than ever before. Remember, building long-term wealth isn't about shortcuts or speculation. It's about taking considered, consistent steps guided by a solid system. To recap, every single time you consider an investment property or not, run through the safer system first. Spend at least an hour really digging deep. Ask yourself, S, is the strategy right for you? A, what will you acquire? How will you acquire the project? F, how will it be funded? E, what about exit? Do you have a plan B, C, D, or even E? Include any partnerships you put in place. R, is the project something you will repeat or should consider repeating? That hour spent running through the system will be priceless longer term. Remember that it's better to regret the projects you miss than those you invest. If you're the impatient type, print that out and put it on your mirror. Make it your phone's screensaver, NB3, whatever it takes to make you stop, breathe, and really consider the investment in the cold, harsh light of day. Need personal support? No one walks into a bookshop, buys a book on surgery, and then operates on their partner's leg.
